name_reason: Compliant fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=pathfind, descriptor=neighbor_step_with_tiebreak. Accurately names the path-aware inner step (direction-recording twin of fd2_flood_fill_neighbor_step @ 0x4E16E) whose distinguishing feature over the plain flood-fill step is the mode-1 direction-diversity tiebreak on a cost tie. No Ghidra address residue; 'tiebreak' is real semantics (mode 1 commit policy), not an ID/dimension to strip.
purpose: Path-aware inner neighbor step of the directional DFS pathfinder: visit one neighbor tile, look up its movement cost via the two-level cost tables, and -- when the new residual cost beats (or in mode 1 ties-then-wins against) the existing marker -- record the branch direction into the tile's direction nibble and conditionally commit the marker, signalling the caller to recurse.
logic_summary: tile_cost = caller_context[ tile_cost_table_ptr[(attr_word & 0x3FF)<<2 + 1] ], where attr_word = *(u16*)(btm_attr_ptr-3). new_cost = remaining_cost - tile_cost (always written to new_cost_out). Gates: (1) if tile_cost > remaining_cost return 0 (too costly); (2) SIGNED compare (int8)new_cost vs (int8)*btm_attr_ptr -- if new_cost < existing return 0; if new_cost > existing compute dir_code = count_unique_directions(); if equal (tie) only mode 1 attempts tiebreak (else return 0), computing dir_code and returning 0 unless dir_code > (*(btm-2) & 0xFC). On commit: pack dir into [-2] preserving its low 2 bits (attr bits 8-9) via [-2] = dir_code | (*(btm-2) & 0x03). Mode 2: write residual marker, *new_cost_out=new_cost, call record_destination_xy(x,y,btm), return 1. Modes 0/1: read flags=*(btm-1); 0x40 impassable -> return 0 (marker withheld but dir already written); 0x80 sink -> new_cost=0; write marker, *new_cost_out=new_cost, call check_destination_save_path(x,y), return 1.
signature: int fd2_pathfind_neighbor_step_with_tiebreak(uint8 x, uint8 y, uint8 remaining_cost, uint8 *btm_attr_ptr, uint8 *new_cost_out)

params.name: x
params.semantics: Neighbor tile X (DL in the binary). Not used by this routine itself; passed through to the destination helpers fd2_pathfind_record_destination_xy / fd2_pathfind_check_destination_save_path.
params.reason: Accurate, no address residue; matches the DL pass-through coordinate.

params.name: y
params.semantics: Neighbor tile Y (DH in the binary). Pass-through to the destination helpers, like x.
params.reason: Accurate, no address residue; matches the DH pass-through coordinate.

params.name: remaining_cost
params.semantics: Residual movement budget at the source tile (CL in the binary); new_cost = remaining_cost - tile_cost and the too-costly gate compares tile_cost > remaining_cost.
params.reason: Descriptive and correct; matches the CL residual budget.

params.name: btm_attr_ptr
params.semantics: Pointer to the neighbor tile's marker byte in the battle tile map (EBX). [-3..-2] = 16-bit attribute word, [-2] = packed direction nibble (attr high byte), [-1] = flags byte, [0] = residual-cost marker.
params.reason: Accurate name describing the BTM attribute/marker pointer; no address residue.

params.name: new_cost_out
params.semantics: Out-parameter receiving the residual cost handed to the neighbor (remaining_cost - tile_cost, forced to 0 for a 0x80 sink in modes 0/1). In the binary this is the CL value the caller feeds into the recursive descent; here it is returned through the pointer.
params.reason: Clear out-parameter name matching its role (Layer-2 stand-in for the CL register result); no address residue.

returns.semantics: Non-zero (1) == binary CLC: neighbor improved, caller should recurse. Zero == binary STC: skip (too costly / not an improvement / tie lost / impassable in modes 0/1).
